title: Interrupt
description: Action: `interrupt`. Stops the agent turn currently running on a conversation — the protocol's Stop button. The running turn is cancelled at its next await point (mid-LLM-stream, or between tool steps) and closes out with a normal `eventual_response`, so clients that predate this action still resolve their streaming state correctly. A turn already interrupted or already finished reports `NO_ACTIVE_TURN`.

Request.title: InterruptRequest
Request.description: Fields sent by the client to stop the running turn. Exactly one of `conversationId` or `sessionId` identifies the target; `conversationId` wins when both are present. A widget typically only holds its `sessionId`, while a reconnected client may hold the conversation directly.

requestId.description: Correlation id for THIS interrupt frame — the server's `immediate_response` ack echoes it. Note this is not the interrupted turn's `requestId`: the cancelled turn closes itself out on its own `requestId`, which is what the client's streaming state is keyed by.

conversationId.description: Conversation whose running turn should be stopped. Preferred when known — turns are tracked per conversation, so this keeps working across a reconnect that minted a new session.

sessionId.description: Session whose conversation's running turn should be stopped. Resolved server-side to the session's `conversationId`. Unknown sessions report `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`.

Response.title: InterruptResponse
Response.description: The server acks with an `immediate_response` (status 200, `data.conversationId`) once the running turn has been signalled. The stop itself surfaces on the INTERRUPTED TURN's `requestId` as an `eventual_response` whose `responseParts` records that the turn was stopped — no dedicated event type, so existing clients need no changes. Errors: `VALIDATION_ERROR` (neither handle given), `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `NO_ACTIVE_TURN` (nothing was running).
